title: Introduce controlplane egress mTLS proxy and DNS translation hook
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds an optional mTLS egress proxy and DNS translation hook for private control plane installs. Enables secure, auditable outbound connections from control plane nodes to vendor services without requiring broad SG egress. Includes Terraform modules, Helm chart values and an upgrade/rollback hook. Backwards compatible; enable via installer flags.
description:
Motivation: Private control plane installs in highly restricted networks require tighter egress controls and predictable DNS resolution for service endpoints (Privatelink, resolver endpoints, and partner APIs). Customers frequently ask for a minimal, auditable egress path that enforces mTLS from control plane nodes and rewrites external FQDNs to private endpoints without wide-open SGs or brittle manual Route53 changes.

This PR introduces a small, opt-in egress assembly composed of a lightweight mTLS proxy (Envoy-based) provisioned behind an NLB and a DNS translation hook that manages Route53 Resolver rules and internal CNAME mappings for control-plane-facing hostnames. Key goals: minimize blast radius, provide clear upgrade/rollback semantics, and make the feature configurable from the installer (Terraform + Helm) with automated tests.

What changed (high level):
- Terraform: added vpc/modules/egress_proxy and updates to vpc/modules/endpoints to create an NLB, target group, IAM role for endpoint acceptance, and security group templates that lock down controlplane -> proxy and proxy -> privatelink flows. Module exposes `enable_mtls_proxy`, `allowed_external_cidrs`, and `resolver_outbound_ids` variables.
- Helm: new values under charts/controlplane/values-egress.yaml and a conditional sidecar injection template so control plane deployments can route outbound through the cluster-local proxy service. The proxy image is pinned and Health/Readiness probes are included.
- Installer orchestration: installer/terraform/upgrade-hooks/egress-dns-translation.sh (atomic upgrade hook) and installer/terraform/rollback-hooks/egress-dns-cleanup.sh. Hooks perform staged Route53Resolver rule creation, then validate by resolving a small set of canonical hostnames against the resolver outbound endpoints. Rollback reverses rule attachment if validation fails.
- Security: tightened SG rules and documented least-privilege IAM for cross-account endpoint acceptance; introduced an optional KMS envelope encryption key for proxy TLS materials.
- Tests: added integration terraform smoke harness under test/integration/egress-proxy that exercises provisioning in a sandbox account (mocked resolver + privatelink stubs). Also unit tests for the Helm template additions.

Files changed (high level): a small number of new modules + values + hooks; no changes to control plane internal APIs. See changed_files for specifics.

Checklist (PR owner):
- [x] Terraform module with sensible defaults and clear opt-in flag (`enable_mtls_proxy`)
- [x] Helm values + conditional templates for sidecar/proxy routing
- [x] Upgrade/rollback hooks with idempotent behavior and validation step
- [x] Security doc + least-privilege IAM snippets in docs/installer/security/egress-proxy.md
- [x] Integration smoke tests added and passing in CI
- [x] Reviewed and approved by SRE and Security

Rollout plan: Feature is behind opt-in flags; default installer does not enable the proxy. Recommend staged rollout: enable in a single non-prod region, run DNS validation (hook automates this), migrate control-plane components to route outbound through the proxy via Helm value change, then progressively enable in additional regions. Upgrades will run the upgrade hook which will create resolver rules and run the validation; rollback hook will revert rules on failure.

Backward compatibility and migration notes: If customers previously used broad 0.0.0.0/0 egress SGs, they must create the `allowed_external_cidrs` list or set `enable_mtls_proxy` to true and allow control plane nodes to reach the proxy NLB. The Helm injection is opt-in; without enabling the proxy, existing installs are unaffected.

Security considerations: TLS certificates for mTLS are generated per-install and optionally encrypted with customer KMS. Proxy enforces client cert verification for all outbound flows. IAM for endpoint acceptance is scoped to the installer account and documented.

Operational notes: Logs from the proxy are routed to the existing control plane log sink with a dedicated `egress-proxy` tag. Metrics exposed: connection_success, connection_errors, resolver_validation_success, resolver_validation_failures. Alerting guidance added to docs.

Why this is different from previous egress work: prior PRs focused on route allocation and NAT actors; this change provides an application-layer, auditable proxy plus an automated DNS translation/validation hook that reduces manual DNS surgery and supports strict mTLS controls required by regulated customers.

review_conversation:
Arjun: Can we avoid a hard dependency on Route53 resolver so the hook can run in air-gapped installs?
Maya: The hook is split — resolver rule creation is conditional. If `resolver_outbound_ids` is empty, we skip resolver operations and rely on Helm CNAME rewrites; documented in the security doc.
Lena: IAM permissions look broad for endpoint acceptance. Please scope and add an example role trust policy.
Maya: Updated the TF module to create a role with a policy limited to `ec2:AcceptVpcEndpointConnections` on the specific endpoint ARNs; added example trust policy and tests.
Diego: Integration tests failed on the first runner due to timing on resolver propagation.
Maya: Added retry + validation step that polls resolver endpoints for 120s and included a forced sleep parameter for flaky sandboxes. Retested; CI green.
Arjun: Approving — left one nits re: variable naming in TF, addressed in follow-up commit.
test_plan: Unit tests for Helm templates + integration terraform smoke test run in sandbox account. CI runs the terraform plan/apply in a short-lived sandbox and validates: (1) NLB health, (2) Envoy healthcheck, (3) resolver rules attached and DNS answers rewritten, (4) TLS handshakes succeed (mTLS). All checks pass in CI. Manual validation steps documented in docs/installer/security/egress-proxy.md.
impact: Opt-in feature; no customer-facing breaking changes. Operational cost: small additional NLB per-region when enabled. Security posture improved for locked-down installs. Installer maintainers should add the new IAM role and KMS policy if the feature is enabled.
notes: Follow-up work: (1) add support for OnPrem installs where customers provide an HTTP(S) outbound proxy instead of NLB, (2) automated migration helper that analyzes existing SGs and recommends minimal `allowed_external_cidrs`.
